one_liner: Meta's Threads REST API (graph.threads.com) for publishing posts, reading replies/mentions and insights; OAuth user tokens, testers work immediately but public users need App Review.
notes: auth: Threads user access tokens via the Authorization Window (OAuth 2.0 authorization code -> short-lived -> 60-day long-lived token) = oauth2. The docs also document app access tokens (client_credentials with Threads app ID + app secret, or passing TH|app_id|app_secret directly), required e.g. for the oEmbed API; that is an app-level key+secret credential with no user grant, labeled other. This 'other' is the ambiguous part: a labeler focused on the main user-data flow would give only [oauth2]. access: self-serve Meta developer app; Threads Testers can grant permissions at any time, but any user without an app role requires each permission to pass App Review and the app to be published -> approval_required / ready_with_review / app_review. mcp: Meta's official MCP servers (Ads, Social Technologies a.k.a. devtools, WhatsApp Business Tools; developers.facebook.com/documentation/mcp) do not mention Threads - devtools manages developer apps/webhooks/doc search, not Threads content - so not counted as an official Threads MCP. Searched developers.facebook.com MCP docs, the Threads docs, fbsamples/threads_api, and the web for 'Threads MCP'; only third-party servers exist (github MetaThreads/meta-threads-mcp, also on PyPI, self-described 'Unofficial'; github baguskto/threads-mcp, pegasusheavy/threads-mcp) -> community. Fetch note: developers.facebook.com TLS-blocks direct curl from this machine; pages were read via a reader proxy and the docs URL now redirects /docs/threads/* -> /documentation/threads/*. breadth moderate: posts/replies/reposts/quotes/insights/profiles/keyword search, no DMs or follow graph.

evidence.quote: API authentication is handled by Threads user access tokens that conform to the OAuth 2.0 protocol.
Use an app access token to make requests to the Threads API on behalf of an app rather than a user.
For app users without a role on your app to grant your app these permissions, each permission must first be approved through the App Review process, and your app must be published.
The Threads API can be accessed by either graph.threads.com or graph.threads.net.
Unofficial MCP server for Meta's Threads API. Enables LLMs like Claude to publish posts, manage replies, and track insights through the Model Context Protocol.
Meta runs official remote Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers that bring Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, and Meta Ads capabilities to your agentic workflows.
